Eamon (Design): Quick question — in the request drilldown header the visible "Copy" icon sits after Close. Keyboard order is weird: Export -> Close -> Copy. Does that match expectations? Ravi (Product): We put Copy on the right for visual alignment but I'm open to moving it. Support likes one-click copy. Ben (Eng-UX): From a flow POV users expect binary actions grouped: primary (Export) then session controls (Close, Copy). Propose DOM order = Export, Close, Copy on desktop; on mobile tuck Copy into overflow. Lily (Eng-Frontend): Current markup has the icon using no `aria-label` and `tabindex="-1"` on the svg wrapper — oops. I'll remove that and make DOM match visual order. Also will ensure icon-only buttons have `aria-label`. Omar (Accessibility): Important: don't rely on tooltip for assistive tech. Use `aria-label="Copy correlation ID"`. Use a live region for confirmation but keep wording short. Prefer: `role="status" aria-atomic="true"` with text "Correlation ID copied." Avoid reading the raw ID. Eamon (Design): Microcopy: primary CTA should read "Download bundle" (users expect attachments) and menu item "Export JSON (raw)". Helper text: "Bundle includes spans, logs, and attachments." Ravi (Product): Agreed. Also avoid changing analytics event names. Add a property `export_variant: bundle|json`. Keep `trace_export.clicked` intact. Lily (Eng-Frontend): Implementation plan: 1) reorder buttons for desktop 2) move Copy into overflow on width < 640px 3) add `aria-label`s and live region 4) bump export button color to pass contrast. Will include color WCAG proof in PR. Omar (Accessibility): For the live region example, please use something like: ```html
Correlation ID copied.
``` Also make sure focus order isn't trapped in the menu; return focus to the menu trigger on close. Ben (Eng-UX): For keyboard UX inside the overflow menu, use roving tabindex and arrow keys to move. Tab should move between top-level controls; Enter opens menu. Standard ARIA menu pattern. Eamon (Design): Small a11y nit: export button uses our orange token which currently fails contrast on white. Can we use token `--brand-strong` or darken by 10%? Lily (Eng-Frontend): I'll try `--brand-strong` and fall back to `#b33b35` if needed. PR will include before/after contrast ratios. ci-bot: FYI: low-risk UI deploy scheduled 03:00-04:00 UTC tomorrow. Ravi (Product): Great. Who picks the PR? Lily (Eng-Frontend): I'll own it. Expect a tiny PR today with screenshots and a 7s keyboard demo. Omar (Accessibility): I'll review and sign off if aria-labels, live region, and contrast evidence are present. Eamon (Design): I'll add updated copy to the PR. Thanks all!
